translationRepairs: In the second year of Taijian (570) he again followed Zhaoda against Xiao Kui at Jiangling. Daoji separately commanded the allied armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud ships, then led Zhaoda's van, took Ancheng, and received its surrender.

In the second year of Taijian (570) he again followed Zhaoda against Xiao Kui at Jiangling. Daoji separately commanded the allied armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud ships, then led Zhaoda's van, took Anshu City, and received its surrender.
攻安蜀城 names Anshu City/fortress; Ancheng drops 蜀 and invents a different place. Anshu City restores the toponym.

In the second year of Taijian he again followed Zhaoda in campaigning against Xiao Kui at Jiangling; Daoji separately commanded the massed armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud fleet, then served as Zhaoda's vanguard, attacked Ancheng, and reduced it.

In the second year of Taijian he again followed Zhaoda in campaigning against Xiao Kui at Jiangling; Daoji separately commanded the massed armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud fleet, then served as Zhaoda's vanguard, attacked Anshu City, and reduced it.
Same unit: 安蜀城 is Anshu City, not Ancheng. The literal replacement matches the Chinese place name.
At the end of Liang's Taiping era Emperor Wen once sheltered at Lin'an. Ya's mother Ling [4] saw his bearing, knew he was no common man, and received him with deep courtesy.
At the end of Liang's Taiqing era Emperor Wen once sheltered at Lin'an. Ya's mother Ling [4] saw his bearing, knew he was no common man, and received him with deep courtesy.
梁太清末 is the end of Liang's Taiqing (太清) era, not Taiping (太平). The proposal wrongly reads 太末 and replaces the era with vague "final years"; restore Taiqing.
At the end of Liang's Taiping era Emperor Wen once took refuge at Lin'an; Ya's mother Ling, saw Emperor Wen's bearing, knew he was no ordinary man, and entertained him with great courtesy.
At the end of Liang's Taiqing era Emperor Wen once took refuge at Lin'an; Ya's mother Ling saw Emperor Wen's bearing, knew he was no ordinary man, and entertained him with great courtesy.
梁太清末 is Taiqing-end, not Taiping or "final years". Keep the comma fix after Ling; name the era Taiqing.
In the third year of Taijian (572) he was made pacifying-distance general and interior administrator of Hengyang. Before he went out he was shifted to administrator of Guiyang.
In the third year of Taijian (571) he was made pacifying-distance general and interior administrator of Hengyang. Before he went out he was shifted to administrator of Guiyang.
太建三年 with Taijian 1 = AD 569 is AD 571. The parenthetical (572) is off by one; (571) is correct.
In the eighth year (577) he returned to court as scattered-cavalry regular attendant on duty in the palace offices.
In the eighth year (576) he returned to court as scattered-cavalry regular attendant on duty in the palace offices.
八年 continues the Taijian reckoning of the preceding sentence; year 8 from 569 is 576, not 577.
In the tenth year (579) he was made inspector of Feng, his other titles unchanged.
In the tenth year (578) he was made inspector of Feng, his other titles unchanged.
十年 under the same Taijian sequence is AD 578 when year 1 is 569; (579) is wrong.
Zilong's nephew Cai had talent and nerve. He campaigned with Zilong, was made administrator of Nanping, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixing [2] with three hundred households.
Zilong's nephew Zicai had talent and nerve. He campaigned with Zilong, was made administrator of Nanping, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixing [2] with three hundred households.
子隆弟子才 gives the nephew's personal name as 子才 (Zicai). English Cai drops 子; Zicai restores the full given name.
